fields.meta_title: Movie Quiz: Play 8 Questions, Build Your Own | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Play an 8-question movie quiz with a source behind every answer, then build one for your own crowd on Emergent. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Movie Quiz Your Crowd Plays on Their Phones
fields.hero_description: Build a movie quiz that scores every team and keeps each answer in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Movie Quiz
fields.features_subheading: A movie quiz tests what a crowd remembers about films. Emergent builds the rounds and scoring, plus a table of every answer.
fields.feature_1:
Questions drafted from your film list

Name a decade, a director, or a list of films, and Emergent drafts multiple-choice questions on them, with wrong choices from the same era. Check each one and change it by prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Rounds with their own scores

Split the quiz into rounds such as 1980s comedies or Best Picture winners. The results screen gives a score for each round, so players see which era they know and which they guessed.
fields.feature_3:
Team play on every phone in the room

Players pick a team on the first screen and answer one question per screen on their own phones. Emergent sets no cap on how many people play, whether that is 7 teams or a full lobby.
fields.feature_4:
Answers kept in a table you own

Each answer is a row in a database you own, tagged with the player, the team, and the night. Sort by question to find the one nobody got, or by team to follow a season of Thursdays.
fields.feature_5:
A Slack message when the round closes

Set a closing time, and the app emails a reminder to anyone who has not finished. When the round closes, the host gets a Slack message with the final standings for each team.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, your code, free to start

Use your venue's domain, included in Emergent and using credits. Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. The free tier covers building and publishing.

fields.hero_prompt: Build a movie quiz on 1990s films for my Thursday bar trivia night that scores 7 teams and shows a leaderboard.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a movie quiz?

quiz_plan.promise: the quiz plays the page's promise: a movie quiz a visitor can take, whose results answer what the H1 says it builds

plan.angle: The top 10 is play-only: question lists, video rounds and quiz games (Land of Trivia, Collider, Sporcle-style categories, YouTube guess-the-film rounds), and none shows a host how to run a quiz for their own crowd. This page lets the searcher play an 8-question movie quiz on the page, each answer tied to a cited fact about a real film, then shows a bar trivia host, a film studies teacher, a film society and an independent cinema running their own quiz as an app that keeps every answer in a table they own.
tab_stories: Harrow Street Taproom runs a 10-question movie round for 7 teams every Thursday, the app totals each team's points after the last question and puts the leaderboard on the bar TV, and the Back Row Crew wins the $40 tab on 9 of 10.

The 28 juniors in Pinecrest High's film studies elective take a 12-question quiz after each week's film, and when 17 of 28 miss question 7 on the opening shot, the teacher replays that scene on Monday.

The Larchmont Film Society sends its 64 members a 6-question quiz before each monthly screening, the last screen is a vote on the next theme night, and 41 members play while noir night takes 23 of the 41 votes.

The Marquee on Fifth, a 2-screen independent cinema, puts a 5-question quiz behind a QR code in its lobby, 312 people play it in October, and the 74 who score 5 of 5 see a free popcorn code on the results screen.
